title: Multi-candidate generate/critique/repair loop with deterministic Python selection
motivation: Single-candidate rule-first prompting has repeatedly produced parseable but exact-wrong programs. ARC-R030 and ARC-R032 showed that removing serialization/parse blockers was not sufficient; ARC-R035 showed the deterministic search space can be large but still miss exact programs. The next architecture hypothesis is that model inference should be used as a diverse proposal engine while Python remains the deterministic judge.

blocking_context.rule: Do not start this protocol until the active T0021/ARC-R036 claim is resolved, unless a later shift explicitly converts this document into a queued task according to RUNNER.md.

hypothesis: A generate -> critique -> repair -> deterministic verification loop can improve candidate coverage versus single-answer rule-first prompting by producing a diverse set of candidate programs and letting Python select strictly by training-pair execution evidence rather than model self-confidence.
primary_variable: Number/diversity of model-generated candidate programs plus critique/repair passes, while keeping the deterministic executor, exact scoring, task set, model/provider policy, and leakage controls fixed.

frozen_comparators.description: single-candidate rule-first overflow ablation; compact serialization; 0/2 exact coverage on 0607ce86 and 06df4c85
schema-v2 lattice-region model ablation; 2/2 parseable but 0/2 exact coverage
no-model bounded overlap-alignment search; 798 reachable states on 0607ce86 but no exact program

initial_task_selection_policy.rationale: ARC-R032 executed lattice programs for this task but produced exact-wrong outputs, making it a good first target for candidate diversity and Python ranking without the current T0021 failure-taxonomy dependency.
initial_task_selection_policy.condition: Use after T0021 classifies the remaining semantic-closure failure modes, or if the queued task explicitly freezes a compatible T0021-derived target mechanism.

diversity_controls: multiple independent prompts or seeds when provider supports it
prompt roles: visual rule, object/region rule, lattice rule, exception rule, minimal program rule
force candidates to be distinct at the normalized IR level
generation.output_format: machine-parseable candidate IR or compact rule text that must be translated into IR before scoring

critique.purpose: Generate failure hypotheses and repair suggestions, not evidence.
required_checks: which training pair is likely to fail
whether the candidate illegally relies on task ID, absolute coordinates, target colors, or target patterns
whether the rule can be expressed in the current IR

critique_the_critique.purpose: Challenge overconfident or incorrect model critiques and recover repairable candidates.
required_checks: is the critique based on actual train-pair evidence or a guessed interpretation
is the candidate repairable without introducing leakage or task-specific constants
does a smaller equivalent rule exist

repair.rule: Repairs may use critique text but must be re-parsed and re-executed from scratch.

python_verifier.authority: Only deterministic Python execution and exact scoring count as evidence.

ranking_order: lower program cost / shorter normalized IR
selector.forbidden: Do not select a candidate because the model says it is best unless Python metrics also rank it best.

model_policy.note: Do not print, persist, or expose provider secrets. If the provider is unavailable, run only no-model harness or scoring work and record the blocker.

leakage_policy.allowed_data: permitted public ARC training data and deterministic public-training-derived development splits only
leakage_policy.forbidden_data: private/sealed evaluation data and repeated public-evaluation feedback
leakage_policy.requirement: All reported candidate scoring must specify split and exact task IDs.

minimum_operational_success: at least 8 parseable, non-duplicate candidates for the selected task
all candidates scored by Python with durable metrics artifact
research_success: >=1 exact train-consistent candidate on the selected task, or
a dominant mechanically observed failure class across all candidates that motivates exactly one next ablation
success_criteria.rejection_condition: If candidate diversity remains high but Python scoring shows no near-miss improvement and no dominant actionable failure class, reject this loop variant and evolve the architecture rather than repeating the same prompt.

required_artifacts: raw sanitized model response cache or hashes
evolution_policy: If the first loop fails, evolve one variable at a time: candidate diversity prompt, critic prompt, repair budget, IR translation constraints, or selector ranking. Preserve matched comparators and do not tune on public evaluation.
